description: The abstract states the paper's own headline conclusion in terms no unit carries: that substantial weak form market inefficiencies are discovered, and that the results shed new light on the January returns earned by prior winners and losers. This is the authors' own summary of the contribution and it is stronger than any sentence in the body.
excerpt: Substantial weak form market inefficiencies are discovered.

description: The abstract states the evidence base and the verdict together -- empirical evidence based on CRSP monthly return data is consistent with the overreaction hypothesis -- which is the single sentence a reader would cite for what the paper concluded. The extraction reaches the same content through the results section but never as the authors' own summary.
excerpt: The empirical evidence, based on CRSP monthly return data, is consistent with the overreaction hypothesis.

description: Figure 1's caption fixes what the main result is a picture of -- cumulative average residuals for winner and loser portfolios of 35 stocks over months 1 to 36, averaged across 16 three-year test periods between January 1933 and December 1980, formation period three years. The extraction has the endpoint numbers but not the window they are drawn from.
excerpt: Figure 1. Cumulative Average Residuals for Winner and Loser Portfolios of 35 Stocks (1-36 months into the test period)

description: The paper's roadmap states that it will discuss the implications for other empirical work on asset pricing anomalies. No unit carries the paper's own statement of its scope, so a reader cannot tell that the small-firm and P/E discussions are promised contributions rather than asides.
excerpt: We discuss the implications for other empirical work on asset pricing anomalies.

description: One unit carries both the Keynes quotation and the Williams quotation. They are separate observations from separate authors and works, each independently citable, and a reader wanting one has to take both.
excerpt: About the same time, Williams noted in this Theory of Investment Value that

description: One unit carries method steps 4 and 5 together. They compute different things -- the pooled two-sample t-statistic for the difference between portfolios, and a one-sample test of whether a single month's average residual differs from zero -- and a replication needs each separately.
excerpt: Similar procedures apply for the residuals of the loser portfolio.

description: The unit reporting that winner and loser portfolios do not differ on market value of equity, dividend yield or financial leverage attributes the result to De Bondt's unpublished dissertation, not to this paper. The same is true of the claim that market model and Sharpe-Lintner results are similar. Read out of context both look like findings of the published study.
excerpt: As shown in-De Bondt [7], the use of market-adjusted excess returns has the further advantage that it is likely to bias the research design against the overreaction hypothesis.
